issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void and instructs orderMeal to call checkOrderReady() with no parameters. The solution implementation defines checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (a one-parameter method) and calls it as checkOrderReady(true). This parameter mismatch contradicts the specification and would confuse students who implement the no-argument method as requested.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's method signature match the specification by changing checkOrderReady(boolean) to checkOrderReady() (no parameters), and update the call in orderMeal to this.checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean parameter if it is intentionally required.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) defines a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void that SealSaloon must implement. In the provided solution SealSaloon, the method is implemented as checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (a different signature). This mismatch in the method interface (same conceptual operation but different parameterization) creates confusion for students: the spec indicates a zero-argument API to call when trying to serve pending orders, but the solution requires providing a boolean flag. Students mapping requirements to implementation may be unsure which signature to implement and how to call it from orderMeal as described in the problem.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution implementation with the problem specification by providing a no-argument checkOrderReady() method. Either: (a) change the solution method signature to public void checkOrderReady() and handle logging internally (e.g., always print or use a class-level flag), or (b) add an overloaded no-arg checkOrderReady() that delegates to checkOrderReady(boolean) so the API required by the exercise matches the implementation. Ensure orderMeal calls the no-arg version as described in the problem.
